source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 10: Inverse of A and A^{-1}A = I_3 (book page 60).

blocks.prompt: 10. Find the inverse of \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ -5 & 0 & 4 \\ 5 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\) and show that \(A^{-1}A = I_3\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein \(3 \times 3\) matrix ka inverse nikalna hai aur phir tasdeeq karni hai ke woh sahi hai.
Inverse woh matrix hai jo \(A\) se multiply ho kar identity \(I_3\) de, bilkul jaise \(5 \times \frac{1}{5} = 1\).
Plan: naun (9) cofactors, \(|A|\), adjoint (cofactors ke matrix ka transpose), \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A\), aur aakhir mein \(A^{-1}A\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ -5 & 0 & 4 \\ 5 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)
Humein find karna hai: \(A^{-1}\), aur dikhana hai ke \(A^{-1}A = I_3\).
Tareeqa: \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A\). Yahan \(\operatorname{adj}A\) cofactors ke matrix ka transpose hai. Inverse tabhi mumkin hai jab \(|A| \neq 0\) ho, is liye pehle determinant dekhenge.

Row 1 ke cofactors
\[A_{11} = +(0 \cdot 0 - 4 \cdot 4) = -16\]
\[A_{12} = -((-5)(0) - (4)(5)) = 20\]
\[A_{13} = +((-5)(4) - (0)(5)) = -20\]
Kyun: Har entry ki row aur column chhupa kar minor, phir signs \(+,\,-,\,+\). \(A_{12}\) mein minor \(-20\) tha, minus lagne se \(+20\).

Row 2 ke cofactors
\[A_{21} = -(2 \cdot 0 - 1 \cdot 4) = 4\]
\[A_{22} = +(1 \cdot 0 - 1 \cdot 5) = -5\]
\[A_{23} = -(1 \cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 5) = 6\]
Kyun: Row 2 ke signs \(-,\,+,\,-\) hain. \(A_{23}\): minor \(4 - 10 = -6\), minus lagne se \(+6\).

\(|A|\) (row 1 ke along)
\[|A| = 1(-16) + 2(20) + 1(-20)\]
\[= -16 + 40 - 20 = 4 \neq 0\]
Kyun: Row 1 ki entries \(\times\) unhi ke cofactors (jo hum nikal chuke). \(|A| = 4 \neq 0\), is liye \(A\) non-singular hai aur inverse maujood hai.

Adjoint (cofactor matrix ka transpose)
\[\operatorname{adj}A = \begin{bmatrix} -16 & 4 & 8 \\ 20 & -5 & -9 \\ -20 & 6 & 10 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Row 1 ke cofactors \((-16, 20, -20)\) column 1 ban gaye, row 2 ke column 2, row 3 ke column 3.\nDhyan dein: Transpose bhool jana sab se aam ghalti hai; cofactors ko seedha likh dein to inverse ghalat aata hai.

Inverse nikalein
\[A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} -16 & 4 & 8 \\ 20 & -5 & -9 \\ -20 & 6 & 10 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix} -4 & 1 & 2 \\ 5 & -\frac{5}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -5 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2} \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj}A\) ki har entry ko \(|A| = 4\) se divide kiya; \(-16/4 = -4\), \(-5/4\) fraction hi rehta hai.

\(A^{-1}A = I_3\) dikhayein
\[(\operatorname{adj}A)A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Adj \(A\) ki row 1 ko \(A\) ke columns se: \(-16 - 20 + 40 = 4\), \(-32 + 0 + 32 = 0\), \(-16 + 16 + 0 = 0\). Row 2: \(20 + 25 - 45 = 0\), \(40 + 0 - 36 = 4\), \(20 - 20 + 0 = 0\). Row 3: \(-20 - 30 + 50 = 0\), \(-40 + 0 + 40 = 0\), \(-20 + 24 + 0 = 4\). Fractions se bachne ke liye pehle adj \(A\) se multiply kiya, phir 4 se divide karenge.

\(|A|\) se divide karein
\[A^{-1}A = \dfrac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = I_3\]
Kyun: \(A^{-1}A = \frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{adj}A)A\); diagonal ke 4 ab 1 ban gaye aur baaqi zero. Yahi identity matrix hai, to hamara inverse sahi hai.
